narrative: An employee was holding a welding rod to clean a pipe on a pump rig so the teeth on the hydraulic chain tongs could have a better grip. His right glove was pulled into the chain tongs, resulting in an amputation of the index fingertip.
issue_messages: 20251111432: the worker was cleaning a machine, which points to control of hazardous energy
specific_regulation_and_reason: Cleaning hydraulic chain tongs: hazardous energy plausible, but NAICS 237110 suggests construction; 1910.147 expressly excludes construction employment. Retained 1910.218 is forging-specific, unsupported by narrative. Confirm activity/jurisdiction and mechanism.

narrative: An employee was pulling a 400-foot run of rope using a wire-pulling machine. After 300 feet of the rope was pulled, it became bound around the capstan. The employee was showing a foreman the issue when the employee's left little finger got pinched between the rope and capstan, resulting in amputation of the finger.
issue_messages: 20251111436: 1910.28 is about falls, but the worker was hurt by machine
specific_regulation_and_reason: Rope pulled around capstan caused finger pinch, not a worker fall. 1910.28 lacks established relevance here; machine nip-point/energization controls and construction rules need investigation. RRI letter inherits the weak citation.

narrative: An employee was walking behind a counter when he tripped on a floor mat and fell to the floor, resulting in hospitalization due to a broken left femur.
issue_messages: 20251111439: a same level fall is 1910.22, not 1910.28
specific_regulation_and_reason: Tripped on mat and fell at same level. 1910.22 walking-working surfaces more relevant than fall-to-lower-level 1910.28; verify specific paragraph and floor-mat facts.

narrative: An employee was disconnecting hoses to a caster segment as a crane was lifting it. A large piece of metal scale fell 7 feet off the caster, striking the employee's left foot and causing a compound fracture.
issue_messages: 20251111443: 1910.28 is about falls, but the worker was hurt by crane load
specific_regulation_and_reason: Metal scale fell from raised crane load onto foot. Worker did not fall, but 1910.28(c) addresses falling-object protection; cannot reject 1910.28 solely because worker did not fall. Confirm precise standard/coverage and appropriate crane rules.

narrative: An employee jumped from the back of a trailer and landed awkwardly on the ground. The employee sustained fractures to their lower left leg.
issue_messages: 20251111449: 1910.28 is about falls, but the worker was hurt by other vehicle
specific_regulation_and_reason: Worker jumped from trailer and fell to ground; the event is a fall. Need distinguish deliberate jump, exposure and applicable 1910 fall protection, not automatically reject for vehicle source.

narrative: An employee was repositioning one of the dies in a 45-ton punch press for setup. The machine operator, who was assisting him, needed to move the foot pedal so he could better position a light to help. When he pushed it out of the way with his foot, the punch press actuated and closed. The press contacted the injured employee's right fingertips, resulting in amputations. The employee was hospitalized.
issue_messages: 20251111462: the worker was setup a machine, which points to control of hazardous energy
specific_regulation_and_reason: Die setup on 45-ton punch press and inadvertent actuation: energy isolation is plausible, but 1910.218 refers to forging machines and is not substantiated by the punch-press narrative. Check whether 1910.217 applies to this power press, plus 1910.147.

narrative: An employee was cleaning a part on a roller machine when his gloved hand was caught in the machine. His right index, middle, and ring fingers were amputated at the tip.
issue_messages: 20251111502: the worker was cleaning a machine, which points to control of hazardous energy
specific_regulation_and_reason: Cleaning roller machine supports 1910.147 investigation; preserved 1910.262 (textile industry) is unsupported for a tubing-services employer. Check machinery type and coverage.

narrative: An employee was working to clean out a clog from a machine when their right thumb and index finger got caught in a roller, resulting in a cut between the thumb and index finger.
issue_messages: 20251111522: the worker was cleaning a machine, which points to control of hazardous energy
specific_regulation_and_reason: Clearing machine clog supports hazardous-energy investigation; preserved 1910.266 governs logging, not established for a textile employer. Verify appropriate guarding standard.

narrative: An employee was using a powered industrial truck to move steel beams in a yard. They were manually adjusting a steel beam on the forks of the truck when the beam fell approximately 2 feet and caught their right hand against the concrete ground. The beam measured 20 inches wide, 34 feet long, and 6 inches in depth. The employee suffered lacerations to four fingers and fractures to the ring and middle fingers.
issue_messages: 20251111525: 1910.28 is about falls, but the worker was hurt by powered truck
specific_regulation_and_reason: Steel beam slipped from powered truck forks, striking hand. Worker did not fall; 1910.28(c) may be relevant only if its falling-object conditions are met, but material handling and powered-industrial-truck requirements require assessment.

narrative: An employee was conducting an inspection inside a railcar. He slipped and fell inside the railcar. He was hospitalized with a broken left femur.
issue_messages: 20251111583: a same level fall is 1910.22, not 1910.28
specific_regulation_and_reason: Worker slipped and fell inside railcar; if same-level, 1910.22 is plausible. Check whether there was an elevation change.

narrative: An employee was responding to a question from another employee. They went to step over a box, tripped on the box, and fell on the floor. The employee's ankle was fractured.
issue_messages: 20251111604: a same level fall is 1910.22, not 1910.28
specific_regulation_and_reason: Worker tripped over box and fell to floor; 1910.22 same-level walking-working surfaces is plausible.

narrative: An employee was performing a maintenance activity on a blower and motor pulley system. The employee was rolling a pulley on the blower motor while pulling a belt to jump the belt off the track. The employee's fingertip was caught between the pulley and the belt, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
issue_messages: 20251111606: the worker was servicing a machine, which points to control of hazardous energy
specific_regulation_and_reason: Removing belt while servicing pulley creates hazardous-energy/nip-point concern; 1910.147 primary and 1910.219 secondary plausible if general-industry application holds.

narrative: An employee was bringing up a valet vehicle. He got out of the truck and the truck reversed, running over his right leg. He sustained ankle pain and injuries to his leg, including a non-displaced transverse fracture of the shaft of his right fibula, resulting in hospitalization.
issue_messages: 20251111613: 1910.178 covers powered industrial trucks, but the vehicle is another kind
specific_regulation_and_reason: Valet truck rolled backward and injured employee. Removing powered-industrial-truck 1910.178 is sound; General Duty Clause is not automatically proven by narrative. Determine feasible specific control and recognized-hazard evidence.

narrative: An employee was using a ladder to hang a display. While coming back down the ladder, she missed the last step and fell to the floor, fracturing her left knee. The employee required surgery.
specific_regulation_and_reason: Worker missed ladder step and fell. 1910.23 ladder standard is a more relevant candidate than 1910.28, which excludes portable ladders from its scope. Verify ladder type.

narrative: An employee was overseeing the operation of a bale press and bagger. There was a broken strap on a bale. The employee went to remove the bale from the bagger. The equipment started automatically and crushed the employee between the bale and the bagger arm. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured pelvis.
issue_messages: 20251111622: 1910.217 covers mechanical power presses, and the narrative does not say the press is one
specific_regulation_and_reason: Bale press/bagger unexpectedly started during bale removal. 1910.217 mechanical press is not proven; replacement 1910.212(a)(3)(ii) may be too specific without point-of-operation evidence. Evaluate servicing and unexpected startup under 1910.147 where applicable.
